== Biography ==
{{African-American Sticker}}
{{Heritage Sticker|ancestors=Native American}}
{{Rhode Island Sticker}}
{{Occupation |image=Black_Heritage_Sticker_Images-28.png|text=was a dressmaker.}}
Lucy E. Glasko was born on January 12, 1846. She is the daughter of [[Glasko-3|Isaac Glasko]] and [[Billings-3866|Mary Billings]]. 
Lucy was born around 1845 to Issac Moody Glasko and Mary with both Native American and African American heritage. <ref>[https://www.google.com/books/edition/After_King_Philip_s_War/LXrgK29zl2QC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Isaac+Glasko&pg=PT344&printsec=frontcover After King Philip's War: Presence and Persistence in Indian New England edited by Colin G. Calloway]</ref>

In the 1850 census Lucy (age 5) was in Griswold, New London, Connecticut, United States.<ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasko-3]] is assessed at 94% (proved). Lucy’s 1850 and 1860 census accounts repeatedly place her as a young child in Isaac M’s Griswold family. The distinctive household identity and consistent mother/family account strongly support Isaac, although the early schedules lack relationship fields.

Confidence concerns this recorded child and the selected father as identified by the held family evidence; maternity and the father’s upstream ancestry are separate.

Next useful test: Inspect Lucy’s birth or later death record naming parents.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M68T-KZM: "United States Census, 1850," database with images, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:M68T-KZM: 19 December 2020), Lucy E Glasko in household of Isaac M Glasko, Griswold, New London, Connecticut, United States; NARA microfilm publication (Washington, D.C.: National Archives and Records Administration, n.d.).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.
